name: Farthing
summary: Farthing serves the faithful from Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. The kind and wise human clergyman guides parishioners and directs aid to settlements across the kingdom.

sections.title: A Bishop in Stormwind
sections.body: Bishop Farthing tends to the spiritual needs of Stormwind City from the Cathedral of Light. Alongside Archbishop Benedictus and the gathered clergy, he counsels travelers, assists those pursuing the holy arts, and attends to the Church of the Holy Light's civic and pastoral duties.

sections.title: Aid to the Plagued Lands
sections.body: From the capital, Farthing directs earnest travelers toward parts of the kingdom in need of holy aid. Reports tell of the necromancer Morbent Fel and an undead blight spreading through Duskwood. Farthing advises on ways to overcome dark sorceries and cleanse the blighted frontier.

faq.q: Where can Bishop Farthing be found?
faq.answer: Bishop Farthing resides inside the Cathedral of Light, at the center of Cathedral Square in Stormwind City.

faq.q: What role does Farthing play in the Cathedral?
faq.answer: Farthing is an ordained bishop in the Church of the Holy Light. He guides visiting faithful, priests in training, and adventurers seeking holy wisdom for distant settlements.

faq.q: How is Farthing involved with Duskwood?
faq.answer: Adventurers dealing with Duskwood's undead menace seek Farthing's advice on the dark arts sustaining the necromancer Morbent Fel. He directs them toward purification.

faq.q: Is Farthing related to other citizens bearing the same name?
faq.answer: Several people across human lands share the Farthing surname, including Coleman and Yvette Farthing. Bishop Farthing does not speak of any direct family ties.

angles.text: As a priest visiting the Cathedral of Light, you can look to Farthing for the hierarchy and scholarly wisdom of Stormwind's human clergy.
As an Alliance adventurer fighting corruption in southern territories such as Duskwood, you can seek divine insight and spiritual resolve from Farthing and his fellow clergy.
